name: Thomas Kinsella

education.notes: Elite Dublin Jesuit secondary school — feeds into Trinity / UCD professional pipeline.

education.degree: BA Management Science and Information Systems Studies (MSISS)
education.notes: MSISS is Trinity's 4-year quantitative business / tech degree blending stats, ops research and IT — strong feeder into Big-4 consulting and finance. Includes an industry placement year.

keyDecisions: Chose MSISS at Trinity — quantitative degree blending stats, ops research and IT, which channelled him toward IT-security consulting rather than pure CS or pure business.
Stayed in Dublin for university — same city as the eventual founding base for Tines.
lessons: Generalist quantitative-tech degrees (MSISS-style) feed naturally into security/data analyst roles at Big 4 firms — a credible non-CS entry into tech.
Trinity + Dublin Jesuit secondary is a strong Irish-establishment network that pays back later in fundraising and hiring.
careerSteps.notes: Pre-iPhone era undergrad; cybersecurity-as-career was still nascent in Ireland at this point.

careerSteps.role: Senior Consultant — IT Security & Digital Forensics
keyDecisions: Joined Deloitte's IT security and digital forensics practice straight out of Trinity — Big-4 training-ground entry point.
Specialised in security/forensics rather than rotating broadly across consulting — narrowed the moat early.
Met Eoin Hinchy here — both were on Deloitte's Dublin security team. The 15+ year co-founder relationship started in this room.
Exited at the ~3-year mark, the canonical optimal Big-4 dwell time before diminishing returns.
lessons: Big-4 consulting can serve as an accelerated apprenticeship into a specific technical niche if you specialise hard inside it, rather than rotating broadly.
Three years is enough to extract the training value and exit upward into an industry operator role with substantially more compounding.
Forensics + security is one of the few Big-4 niches where technical credibility transfers cleanly to product companies later.
Your future co-founder may already be sitting next to you at your first job — Kinsella + Hinchy's Tines partnership traces back to Deloitte Dublin in 2008.
careerSteps.notes: Cybersecurity was becoming a distinct discipline; Deloitte forensics was one of few structured entry points in Ireland. Hinchy was on the same team — the founding relationship began here, not at DocuSign.

keyDecisions: Moved client-side to eBay's eCrime team — first-party security operator role at a marketplace facing real adversaries at industrial scale.
Led EMEA investigations team, working directly with global law-enforcement agencies (FBI, Europol, Interpol) on high-impact threats.
Followed/overlapped with Eoin Hinchy at eBay — second of three companies where they worked together before Tines.
Stayed in Dublin (eBay's EMEA hub) — kept Irish operating base while gaining US-scale exposure to product and tooling.
lessons: Moving from consultancy (Deloitte) to first-party operator (eBay) is where you actually feel the pain points that later become product ideas — consultants see symptoms, operators see causes.
Public-private interface roles (working with law enforcement) build a kind of credibility that pays back hard in B2B security sales later.
Choosing a multinational's local HQ (eBay Dublin) lets Irish operators get US-scale experience without emigrating.
careerSteps.notes: Mobile-cloud era; marketplace fraud was becoming an industrial-scale problem and security-ops tooling was largely manual runbooks and ticketing — the exact pain Tines later automates.

keyDecisions: Joined DocuSign as Senior Director, Security Operations — leadership seat at a then-pre-IPO SaaS scale-up (DocuSign IPO'd April 2018).

Re-united with Eoin Hinchy (who led European security ops / incident response at DocuSign, including the 145M-user-record breach) — third company they worked together at, now both at senior leadership level.

Lived the manual-SOC pain firsthand: alert fatigue, runbook sprawl, repetitive triage across dozens of tools. Identified 'three big problems in security: too much work, too many alerts, not enough staff'.
Left DocuSign in early 2018 to co-found Tines — exited the operator chapter ~3 months before DocuSign's IPO.
lessons: Director-level seat at a soon-to-IPO SaaS company gives you both pre-IPO equity and operator credibility — a near-ideal launchpad to founding.
The best B2B SaaS ideas are often the ones you wished existed at your last job; Tines is exactly that for SecOps automation.
Co-founder relationships compound across companies — Kinsella + Hinchy stacked 10 years of shared context across Deloitte → eBay → DocuSign before founding.
Two senior operators co-founding around a domain they both ran is a substantially de-risked founding configuration vs. one operator + one outsider.
careerSteps.notes: DocuSign IPO'd April 2018 — Kinsella exited around founding time, so likely captured some pre-IPO equity upside; the partnership with Hinchy spans Deloitte (2008+), eBay, then DocuSign — the load-bearing pattern is durable cross-company co-founder pairing, not one-off SOC overlap.

careerSteps.role: Co-founder; COO then Chief Customer Officer (Nov 2022)
keyDecisions: Co-founded Tines with Eoin Hinchy in 2018 in Dublin — no-code/low-code automation platform for security and IT teams.

Initially took COO seat at founding; transitioned to Chief Customer Officer in November 2022 as the company scaled — explicit split based on Hinchy/Kinsella's complementary strengths (product/eng vs. customer/community).
Co-headquartered in Dublin and Boston, retaining Irish operating base while planting US revenue flag.
Raised through Accel, Felicis, CrowdStrike's growth fund, Addition; Series C in 2024 at ~$1.125B post-money valuation (unicorn status).
Built a content/community-led GTM (The Future of Security Operations podcast, Dark Reading writing) — leveraged operator credibility into market presence.
lessons: Operator-turned-founder at age 32 with 10+ years of security-ops scar tissue is a high-percentage starting position — the antithesis of the 19-year-old-dropout narrative.
Splitting CEO/CCO roles between co-founders lets each play to strength; Kinsella drove the customer-and-community side that defined Tines' market presence.
Dual Dublin/Boston HQ is a viable structure for Irish/NI founders selling to US enterprise — keep Irish operating cost base, plant US revenue flag.
Pre-IPO operator equity + founder equity stacking is a low-key path to 10-100M outcomes without unicorn-scale risk.
careerSteps.notes: AI-revolution era; SOAR/security-automation category re-energised by the AI agent narrative. Tines crossed unicorn valuation in May 2024 ($50M Series C extension at $1.125B).

exitEvents.notes: Tines $50M Series C extension (May 2024) at $1.125B post-money valuation; cumulative funding >$146M. Paper wealth, pre-exit.

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-founder and Chief Customer Officer of Tines (Dublin/Boston); hosts The Future of Security Operations podcast; recognised voice in cybersecurity automation.

lessons.lesson: Operator-to-founder route works best when the last operator job was the one where you felt the product gap most acutely (DocuSign SOC → Tines).
Founders with deep operator experience in the problem domain (10+ years in security ops) build more credible and useful tools than outsiders.
Irish founders can credibly build US-enterprise SaaS by structuring dual-HQ (Dublin operating, Boston/SF revenue) — Tines is the template for NI/Ireland B2B SaaS.
Choose the right title at founding — Chief Customer Officer signalled where his comparative advantage lay vs. the CEO co-founder. Title-as-honest-signal of comparative advantage.

Co-founder durability comes from cross-company overlap, not single-company overlap: Kinsella + Hinchy worked together at Deloitte (~2008), eBay, AND DocuSign before founding Tines. 10+ years of stacked context.

notes: AI/automation-era cybersecurity founder; operator-turned-founder archetype with a Dublin/Boston dual-HQ that is highly applicable as a model for European (incl. NI/Ireland) B2B SaaS founders building from domain expertise. The load-bearing turning point is the *cross-company* Hinchy partnership (Deloitte → eBay → DocuSign → Tines), not just a single SOC overlap. Kinsella was COO until Nov 2022 when he transitioned to Chief Customer Officer. Specific role start/end years are partly inferred from typical career timing.

firstCompany.name: Tines
firstCompany.oneLiner: No-code/low-code automation platform for security and IT teams; founded in Dublin with Eoin Hinchy after 10+ years of stacked context across Deloitte → eBay → DocuSign. Unicorn at $1.125B (May 2024).
